lab.title: Build, inspect, archive, restore
lab.scenario: Practice a complete file lifecycle. The restore step is what proves the backup actually worked.

steps.text: Create a project tree with three subdirectories.
Create three dated notes using brace expansion.
steps.verify: ls ~/lab/fieldbook/notes should show day1.txt, day2.txt, and day3.txt.

steps.text: Add a line to the first note and inspect its metadata.
steps.verify: stat should show a non-zero size and a recent modification time for day1.txt.

steps.text: Archive the notes directory with gzip and list the archive.
steps.verify: You should see notes/, notes/day1.txt, and the others.

steps.text: Restore the archive into a clean directory and compare.
steps.verify: diff should print nothing. Silence means the trees match.

quiz.q: Which cp option best preserves ownership, permissions, timestamps, and links?
quiz.why: Archive mode (-a) combines recursive copying with metadata preservation. It is the right default for backups.
t lists, z handles gzip, f names the archive file. Listing first is a safe inspection step.

quiz.q: Why is rm -rf with an unquoted variable dangerous in a script?
options: An empty variable can turn the target into a broader path
It always deletes the home directory
quiz.why: If the variable is empty, the path can collapse. Quoting plus set -u prevents the worst case.
